column2: A technique that carves a continuous recording into overlapping fixed-length chunks, so each chunk becomes one sample.
How far a sliding window advances between one sample and the next.
Information from the test set influencing training, which inflates the reported score and makes it meaningless.
A value you choose before training, such as window length, number of trees, or learning rate.
A value the model learns by itself during training, such as a network weight or a tree split threshold.
Constructing new input variables from existing ones because you believe they express the underlying phenomenon more directly.
Rescaling a feature so it has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Of all the cases the model called positive, the fraction that were actually positive.
Of all the genuinely positive cases, the fraction the model caught.
F1 computed separately for each class, then averaged with equal weight given to each class.
The unweighted mean of per-class recall.
Training many models on random subsamples of the data and averaging their votes, so their individual errors cancel.
Training models sequentially, where each new model is fit to the errors the previous ones are still making.
Randomly zeroing a fraction of neurons at each training step, so the network cannot depend on any single pathway.
Not observing the event of interest for a subject because the study ended before it happened.
Creating labels from the data itself, such as masking part of a signal and training the model to reconstruct it.
